messages:
alex: Heads up — we've had 4 GPU training jobs land on the general-purpose nodepool this morning even though the pods have nodeAffinity + tolerations for the gpu pool. cost spike incoming :grimacing:

maria: ugh. do you have the Pod yaml + node labels?

alex: pasted the key bits below: 
```yaml
nodeAffinity:
  requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
    nodeSelectorTerms:
    - matchExpressions:
      - key: accelerator
        operator: In
        values: [nvidia-t4]
tolerations:
- key: "gpu-pool"
  operator: "Exists"
  effect: "NoSchedule"
```
Nodes are labelled: `accelerator=nvidia-t4` on gpu-pool nodes, and gpu-pool nodes are tainted `gpu-pool=dedicated:NoSchedule`.

sam: can you `kubectl describe pod` for one of the mis-scheduled pods? also paste `kubectl get nodes --show-labels` for both pools

alex: here — short excerpt from describe: 
```
Events:
  Normal  Scheduled  2m  default-scheduler  Successfully assigned default/train-job-23 to general-3
  Warning FailedScheduling  2m  default-scheduler  0/6 nodes are available: 3 node(s) didn't match nodeSelector, 3 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate.
```

kelly: Wait that says 'didn't tolerate' — but you showed tolerations. Is the toleration key/value right? you used operator: Exists so it should tolerate any key presence.

alex: I double-checked the live yaml — the kustomize overlay was stripping the tolerations for some environments. so the pods hitting general pool had no toleration at all; but still weird: some pods with toleration are still ending up on general nodes.

maria: Two quick things to check: 1) Are the taints exactly the same string? `kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[*].spec.taints}'` — sometimes we have `gpu-pool=true:NoSchedule` vs `gpu-pool=dedicated:NoSchedule`. 2) NodeAffinity uses `In` vs stray whitespace on values.

alex: confirmed: occasional mismatch existed earlier (we had `dedicated` vs `reserved` labels historically), fixed that. But the odd ones look like CA behaviour: cluster-autoscaler spun up a general node and scheduler bound the pod before taints were applied on that node. logs show creation -> scheduling -> kubelet taint injection delay?

sam: CA can race: taints are applied at node bootstrap; if a node appears in API without taints, scheduler might place pods on it. We avoid this by setting the cloud-init/instance-template to include taints at creation, or by using `--register-with-taints` on kubelet. Which cloud provider?

alex: GCP. Our nodepool template uses startup-script to `kubectl taint` in a post-bootstrap step — too late.

maria: ok that explains it. Options: 1) add `--register-with-taints` to kubelet args so taint present on registration, 2) make the scheduler wait using `PodToleratesNodeTaints` (not configurable), or 3) add a mutating webhook that injects tolerations (not ideal).

kelly: For immediate mitigation we can: a) add admission webhook to enforce tolerations on GPU workloads, b) update nodepool startup to set taints earlier, c) use nodeAffinity + requiredDuringScheduling to strongly prefer correct nodes (but not bulletproof).

alex: Another wrinkle — cluster-autoscaler is scaling up the wrong nodepool sometimes (p4 pool instead of t4) because our CA expander policy chooses cheapest/closest. When a pod has nodeAffinity for `accelerator=nvidia-t4`, CA should prefer the t4 pool. I think CA only uses resource requests not nodeAffinity when deciding which nodeGroup to create.

sam: yep CA doesn't always honor nodeAffinity when choosing nodegroup. We can add `node.kubernetes.io/instance-type` and explicit resources to the t4 pool and annotate autoscaler with `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-down-disabled=false`? also CA has `--balance-similar-node-groups` and `--skip-nodes-with-local-storage` flags that affect decisions but not affinity.

maria: Proposal: tag the t4 nodepool with `cloudprovider.k8s.io/nodegroup=gpu-t4` and enable CA auto-discovery with `--nodes` range for that group. Also ensure pods request a fake resource like `nvidia.com/gpu: 1` so CA knows it's GPU-bound.

kelly: +1 on the fake resource; we already request `nvidia.com/gpu: 1` for these jobs right?
alex: yes we do. But some older cronjobs don't request GPUs (they relied on nodeAffinity alone). I'll roll a quick audit to find pods without GPU resource requests.

k8s-bot: Headline: 3 nodes created in gpu-t4-pool at 08:23 UTC, taints applied at 08:23:45 (3/3).

maria: action items:
- alex: audit 24h of pods with nodeAffinity but without `nvidia.com/gpu` resource and fix manifests by EOD
- infra: update GKE nodepool templates to set taints at registration or use `--register-with-taints`
- sam: verify CA discovery flags and ensure CA can prefer gpu-t4 nodegroup (maybe via `--expander=priority` and annotating nodegroups)

alex: I'll start the audit and push a hotfix to kustomize overlays that were removing tolerations. Also putting a quick admission check for the short term.

kelly: Also let's add a Grafana alert: if pods with `nvidia.com/gpu` land on nodes without `accelerator` label, fire pager during business hours. cost alerting + oncall notification.

maria: agree. last thought — for region/zone constraints: if t4 pool only in us-west and CA tries to spin up p4 in eu-west because of quota, we need to add topologySpread or nodeAffinity to avoid cross-region scaleups. keep that in mind while you audit.

alex: thanks all, starting now. will post updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
